title: Commodity-specific critical minerals evidence for future systems
question: Which materials are binding for chips, grids, batteries, defense, and AI infrastructure?
why_it_matters: Critical minerals matter differently across systems. FTFN needs commodity-specific evidence before treating a material as a binding constraint.
current_support: FTFN has USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries as an official baseline source, an in-review critical materials signal, DOE critical-materials program context, and a selected Grants.gov funding-opportunity record for processing scale-up.
candidate_records: DOE Critical Minerals and Materials Accelerator opportunity
next_action: Watch DOE selections and pair any award with USGS, trade, permitting, production, offtake, and facility records before treating a material as a binding system constraint.
notes: Phase 50 added a bounded DOE/Grants.gov funding signal, but the gap remains open until commodity-specific supply, processing, trade, production, recycling, and offtake evidence is selected.
